# share.notambourine.com

Private artifact sharing. Upload a file or folder, get an unguessable branded
URL, hand it to one person. This file is the whole API.

## Auth

Writes need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: either your raw vault token or a
short-lived session token (see Session). Load the raw token from 1Password by
reference; never paste it into a transcript or a shell history. Convention:
it lives in your Employee vault as item `share-token`, field `credential`.
Run a raw-token command under this prefix (op run resolves the reference from
the environment; single-quote the inner command so your shell does not expand
$SHARE_TOKEN early):

    SHARE_TOKEN=op://Employee/share-token/credential op run -- sh -c '<command>'

Reads need nothing: the unguessable hash in the URL is the credential.
Signed-tier artifacts additionally need a `/k/<token>/` path segment.

## Session

Trade the vault token for a session token once, then run every upload with
the session token and no 1Password unlock:

    curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      https://share.notambourine.com/session

Returns 201 {token, name, expiresAt}. ttl defaults to 5m (?ttl=, cap 1h).
Convention: write the response to ~/.cache/notambourine-share/session.json
(mode 0600) and read the token from there per upload, AWS-STS-cache style,
so the token never enters a transcript or shell history.
The session token authorizes /up only: list, delete, and signing an older
artifact still need the vault token, and a session cannot mint another
session, so an exfiltrated session token caps at a few minutes of uploads.
A signed-tier upload returns its own link (see Upload), because signing what
you just created spends no authority beyond the upload itself. A 401 here
means the server rejects your vault token itself. An expired session 401s
with "session expired" on upload; mint a new one and retry.

## Upload

    curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      -F f=@out/report.html https://share.notambourine.com/up/<space>

Returns the share URL as plain text (`Accept: application/json` for JSON).
Multiple `-F f=@...` fields keep their relative paths, so a folder with an
`index.html` serves as a real page with its own CSS, JS, and images.

Query parameters:
  tier=open|signed   default open; signed requires a minted /k/ token to view
  ttl=<dur>|forever  fixed artifact expiry, default 90d (e.g. 7d, 12h, 4w)
  idle=<dur>         expire this long after last access instead of a fixed date
  sign=<dur>|forever signed tier only: link life, default 30d
  short              signed tier only: also mint a /z/<id> shortlink

A signed-tier upload returns the signed link, not the bare one, because the
bare one 401s. With `Accept: application/json` it comes back as signedUrl,
signedExp, and short, alongside url and hash. The JSON answer also carries
adminUrl and adminExp: the artifact's admin link (see Admin link), live for
5 minutes, for the uploader only - never a link to hand over. The plain-text
answer stays the one hand-over URL.

## Re-sign an older artifact

    curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"path":"<space>/<hash>","ttl":"30d","short":true}' \
      https://share.notambourine.com/sign

Returns {url, exp, short?}. ttl defaults to 30d; "forever" never expires.
short:true also mints a /z/<id> shortlink that 302s to the signed URL.

## Admin link

    curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      https://share.notambourine.com/<space>/<hash>/admin

Returns {url, exp}: the artifact's admin link, live for 5 minutes. Upload
mints one too (adminUrl in its JSON answer); this route re-opens it. The url
carries ?c=<token>, a credential scoped to exactly this artifact's config and
delete routes - it is not a view token and never belongs in a link you hand
over. It authorizes two writes:

    POST /<space>/<hash>/config?c=<token>    {"ttl":"30d"} or {"ttl":"forever"}
    DELETE /<space>/<hash>/?c=<token>        same soft delete as Revoke below

The config write answers {c, expiresAt}: a fresh 5-minute token (each edit
restarts the clock; adopt the new c) and the expiry it committed. The ttl
counts from upload and takes over expiry entirely, clearing any idle rule; a
ttl the artifact has already outlived counts from the write instead.

Opened in a browser, the url serves an admin page: format links to hand over
(they carry no c=), the expiry chips, and delete. An invalid or expired c=
serves the plain view, never a 401.

## List a space

    curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      https://share.notambourine.com/<space>/

JSON array, newest first: hash, url, tier, uploader, createdAt, expiresAt,
idleTtl, expired, files (count), bytes. Times are epoch seconds; expiresAt
null means no fixed expiry. Without the Bearer header this path returns 404.

## Revoke

    curl -sS -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      https://share.notambourine.com/<space>/<hash>/

Soft delete: the upload moves to trash and purges 90 days later. The live
link dies within 10 minutes (cache lifetime).

## Viewing

The same URL renders for browsers and serves raw bytes to everything else
(curl, <img src>, Slack unfurls). Overrides: ?raw forces bytes, ?view forces
the branded shell, ?view=source shows
uploaded HTML highlighted instead of executed.

Decks render with Marp. --- splits slides, and Marp directives apply:
<!-- _class: lead --> centers a title slide, <!-- paginate: true --> numbers
them. Arrow keys move between slides and the #n fragment links to one.

## Formats

Swap a markdown share URL's extension for a branded export: uploaded
`deck.md`, ask for `deck.pdf`. A suffix decides the output on its own, so
Accept gets no vote, and a file uploaded under the suffixed name always wins
over the export.

    deck.md              branded page, deck or document decided from the content
    deck.txt             the source, text/plain, always
    deck.html            the same page, at a URL that carries an extension
    deck.slides.html     branded page, always a deck
    deck.doc.html        branded page, always a document
    deck.pdf             PDF, deck or document decided from the content
    deck.slides.pdf      PDF, always a deck
    deck.doc.pdf         PDF, always a document

Bare .md, .pdf, and .html read the content to choose: `marp: true` front matter
or `---` slide separators mean deck, anything else means document. Name
.slides.* or .doc.* when you want to decide instead of guessing. When one
upload holds both deck.md and deck.markdown, the .md spelling wins the base
name.

The .html spellings are pages, not downloads: the Worker renders them on the
request that asks, so they answer immediately and pick up a brand change with no
re-render. Only the PDFs are stored artifacts.

An uploaded HTML page exports too: uploaded `page.html`, ask for

    page.pdf             PDF of the page, plain A4
    page.png             screenshot, the whole page at 1280 wide
    page.full.png        the same object, spelled out
    page.browser.png     screenshot, above the fold, 1280x720

PNG is HTML-only; markdown keeps its own family above. When one upload holds
both deck.md and deck.html, markdown wins the base and deck.png is a 404.

Nothing renders at upload. A .pdf or .png is rendered by the first request that
asks for it and then cached, so that request can take a few seconds; one that is
not rendered yet answers 202 with Retry-After: 5 - wait that long and
re-request. It never answers HTML at 200, so `curl -o` cannot write a page into
a .pdf.

## Skill

GET /SKILL.md is a drop-in Claude skill covering all five verbs.
